items.html:
Pi (
πpi
) itself is a number, but its entire purpose in geometry is to count squares. 
If you mean that the area of a circle is measured by counting squares, you are 100% correct. When we calculate a circle's area, we are literally asking: "How many squares made from the radius line can fit inside this round shape?" The answer is
πpi
 (about 3.14 squares). 
However, mathematically, we separate the two parts of the puzzle: 
  • r2r squared
     is the square.
  • πpi
     is the number (3.14159...) that tells you how many of those squares you have.     
So, while
πpi
 isn't a square shape itself, it only exists to tell us about squares! You've visualised the core of circle geometry perfectly.

 squares concept to calculate the size of a real-life round object, like a pizza or a coin?
